newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends week up on support.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends week up on support.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures rose for the fifth day in a row on Friday on institutional support, despite a mild correction in the morning, traders said.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at 23,310 yuan ($2,810) per tonne, rising 180 yuan. It opened at 23,080 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 23,000 and a high of 23,330.
March rose 150 to 22,950, April 230 to 23,180, June 170 to 23,300, July 180 to 23,300 and August 110 to 23,300.
Combined volume fell to 35,420 tonnes from 71,580.
Copper opened lower on profit-taking but institutional buying late in the session, supported by firmer spot prices, pushed most contracts to close near their intraday highs, traders said.
"Institutions were taking advantage of firmer spot prices to squeeze short-position holders," one trader said.
"Many investors believed copper would not fall sharply despite possible technical corrections, helping copper rebound from the day's lows," he added.
Traders said the mid-term trend was optimistic with market sentiment improving.

"After sharp gains in the past week, investors gradually came out from beneath the shadow of a bearish market and many of them preferred to build fresh long positions while prices were low," a second trader said.
Analysts said a deeper correction was unlikely given hot market sentiment and they said they expected copper to remain strong in the short term.
Aluminium ended unchanged. The only traded May 1997 closed at 16,000 yuan per tonne, unchanged from Thursday's close after 150 tonnes traded.
